question_text: Explain why an organization should review firewall rules before allowing incoming connections to a new file-sharing service.
adaptation_rationale: Retain exposed-service risk with explicit firewall/vulnerability reasoning; do not teach every opened port is automatically compromised. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
solution: Permitting connections exposes the service to external clients; an unpatched or insecure service may be exploited. Restricting allowed traffic to necessary sources/services reduces exposure, but a firewall does not repair the application’s vulnerabilities.

marking_points.criterion: Allowed incoming connection exposes a service.
Connects exposed insecure/unpatched software to exploitation risk.
Firewall rules reduce exposure but do not fix software flaws.
